title: Common-Cause Failure Analysis of an LLM 'Ensemble' Borrowing the Knight-Leveson N-Version Method

original_idea.body:
# Common-Cause Failure Analysis of an LLM Ensemble

Replicate the Knight-Leveson independence test on ~8 open models over labeled binary safety judgments; statistically test whether coincident multi-model failures exceed independence and quantify the common-cause-failure surplus. Inference + statistical test.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Level 4: strong chain — rigorous independence test of LLM-ensemble safety guardrails, tied to cascading-failure concentration risk.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Level 4: run ~8 models on labeled judgments and apply the classic coincident-failure test; well-defined inherited method.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Level 5: tightly scoped single experiment (coincident-failure surplus vs independence) with clear statistical criteria.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Level 4: public models + labeled data, weak lab incentive, audits a widely-assumed mitigation.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference + statistical test, near CPU-level aggregation.

novelty.reasoning: Applying Knight-Leveson rigor to LLM ensembles appears largely novel.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: No known rigorous N-version independence test on LLM safety ensembles.
